issues.legal_issue: The court’s discretion to condone delay in filing an appeal under Section 5 of the Limitation Act is conditional on sufficient cause and may be declined where the delay is inordinate or the applicant was negligent or failed to act with due diligence.
A liberal or justice-oriented approach to condonation of delay cannot override the mandatory bar on time-barred appeals under Section 3 of the Limitation Act.
Delay in filing an appeal cannot be condoned merely because similarly situated litigants received relief or because conditions are imposed to exclude benefits for the period of delay.
The merits of the proposed appeal are not to be considered when deciding an application to condone delay.
The High Court was justified in refusing to condone the delay in filing the proposed appeal in the circumstances of the case.
